15: Ippo Makunouchi is the main protagonist of the series. He lives with his mother, Hiroko Makunouchi, and helps with the family charter boat fishing business.
845: Takamura is very hearty, rude and often behaves vulgarly.
846: Aoki was a punk from his childhood up through high school, at which point he encountered, fought and got beat down by Takamura Mamoru (who was then a middleweight with two wins under his belt).
847: Ippo's senpai and Aoki's best friend. He is the smooth, collected type and a romantic at heart, but trains as hard as anyone. His style incorporates a fast left and faster footwork.
1817: Mashiba Ryo is one of the darker characters in the series, but has shown his lighter and good natured side from time to time. He lives with his sister, Kumi Mashiba, whom he is very protective of. Their parents are deceased, having died in an accident when Mashiba was in school.
1818: Kumi is Ryo Mashiba's sweet-natured, but hard-working and willful younger sister, and as such understands him better than anyone else.
1821: Sendo is an In Fighter with arm strength on par with Ippo Makunouchi. To date, he is the only boxer to face Ippo more than once in the pro ring and is his chief rival. Sendo is a featherweight and his most well known move is his powerful smash.
4057: Yamada was a weakling who, like his Kamogawa gym sempai Ippo, was often bullied. He was given the nickname Gero-michi because of his tendency to vomit whenever pushed physically.
4110: Ever since he was little, Miyata has always wanted to be like his dad. His dad, Suzuki Miyata, used to be a boxer, until a career-ending jaw bone injury forced him to retire.
5177: At an age swiftly approaching thirty, Date is an old-timer for a boxer but is nevertheless the man that Ippo looks up to. Years ago, he lost his World Title Match to the champion, Ricardo Martinez, who was defending his title for the 2nd time.
5184: The most recent addition to the roster, the charming Manabu has a prodigy's talent and was the captain of his high school's boxing team.
10156: Head coach and founder of the Kamogawa gym. He fought as a prizefighter in Japan shortly after the end of World War II.
10446: The World Amateur Champion is a handsome boxer from Russia who excels at outboxing and taking points, but adopts a vicious infighting style when he moves to Japan (Ippo notices how depressed he looks after this happens). Raised by a single mother in a small town near to St.
12796: Umezawa was originally the leader of Ippo's bullies at high school, but later became a fan of his after he became a pro boxer. During high school he would wear his hair in a pompadour style, a trademark of many Japanese delinquents.
15841: Ricardo Martinez is currently the only 'Super Champion' in the series. He has the longest title run in the series, with 21 defenses of his WBA Featherweight Title over a decade. He became WBA Featherweight Champion at the age of 21.
15861: Sawamura is a boxer and counter-punch user who is naturally talented, but likes to cause his opponents pain in the ring, which often disqualifies him.
15978: Yagi is the manager of the Kamogawa Gym and a contemporary of Miyata's father. His duties primarily consist of publicity and match booking, but he also takes part in managing the finances, selling merchandise, and occasionally even assists with the training now and then.
17569: An American boxer, the WBC Junior Middleweight champion, who is most likely based off of the semi-retired British boxer, Naseem Hamed.
19267: A 23-year-old sportswriter who works alongside Fujii. Iimura's calm indifference and sharp wit serve often to put off those who would judge her only for beauty, but she is an avid boxing fan and, though less experienced than some, an outstanding journalist.
30130: The defining voice of the Ippo franchise, the ring announcer is with us throughout every liver blow, gazelle punch, and Dempsey roll of every match.
34715: Nekota Ginpachi is a long time friend and eternal rival of Kamogawa Genji. He lives as a hermit in the mountains with his dog Hachi. Nekota is still very much involved in boxing.
36882: Ichiro Miyata's father and coach, and the one who passed on to him the love of boxing. He is a former a Japan and OPBF champion and considered a world contender when he was in his prime.
36885: Fujii is a veteran reporter who often knows about any given boxer's current situation. He has been following Makunouchi Ippo's career since his second spar with Miyata Ichirou and could possibly be viewed as Ippo's first fan.
37320: The longtime rival of Itagaki Manabu, Imai was the one boxer who managed to thwart Itagaki in his high-school days. They fought a total of three times in the amateur ring; each time Imai was victorious.
51817: Tomiko is a nurse who works in the same hospital as Kumi and is also Aoki's girlfriend. She is very kind and very devoted to Aoki, usually assaulting anyone who picks on him or laughs during his matches. She has even stood up to Takamura before.
51821: Date Eiji's Wife. She strongly supports his boxing career and even helped push him back into it after he temporarily retired.
51823: Eiji Date and Date Aiko's second son.
66311: A 16 year old high school student at introduction, Nanako is one of Makunouchi Ippo's biggest fans. Because of this, she views Mashiba Kumi as a rival and competes with her at almost everything.
210065: Yuki met Kamogawa Genji and Nekota Ginpachi at a boxing match in the 1940s. She befriended and lived with Kamogawa Genji and Nekota Ginpachi in their youth.
258844: A former American sergeant and a world-class professional boxer, who was the main antagonist of the Post-War Arc. He largely underestimated Japanese fighters.
